extraction.name: SQuAD (Stanford Question Answering Dataset)
extraction.description: A reading comprehension dataset consisting of 107,785 question-answer pairs posed by crowdworkers on 536 Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text (span) from the corresponding reading passage.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Dataset collected in three stages: (1) curating passages from top 10000 Wikipedia articles by PageRank, sampling 536 articles and extracting paragraphs; (2) crowdsourcing question-answer pairs via the Daemo platform (Amazon Mechanical Turk backend) where workers asked and answered up to 5 questions per paragraph; (3) collecting at least 2 additional answers for each question in development and test sets via a secondary crowdworker task.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Questions deemed unanswerable by span in the paragraph were submitted without an answer marked; 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one additional crowdworker.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Top 10000 English Wikipedia articles ranked by Project Nayuki's Wikipedia internal PageRanks, from which 536 articles were sampled and 23,215 paragraphs (≥500 characters, excluding images, figures, tables) were extracted.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers on Daemo/MTurk were required to have 97% HIT acceptance rate, minimum 1000 HITs, and be located in US or Canada. Workers asked to spend 4 minutes per paragraph, paid $9/hour. Task: ask and answer up to 5 questions per paragraph, with answers highlighted in text. Copy-paste was disabled to encourage original wording. Additional answer collection task had workers select shortest span answering each question, at 5 questions per 2 minutes.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 2.6% of questions in dev and test sets were marked unanswerable by at least one additional crowdworker. Manual labeling of 192 examples for reasoning categories was performed. Syntactic divergence was automatically measured using edit distance between dependency paths.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 5 question-answer pairs per paragraph for primary annotation; at least 2 additional answers per question in development and test sets
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Located in the United States or Canada; minimum 97% HIT acceptance rate; minimum 1000 HITs completed
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP used for constituency parses, POS tags, and NER tags to automatically categorize answer types and measure syntactic divergence
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has a ceiling on accuracy due to constituent parsing constraints, with only 77.3% of correct answers being constituents. Some questions are ambiguous or do not have unique answers (6.1% of sampled examples).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for reading comprehension and natural language understanding research, including training and evaluating question answering models.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Articles were partitioned randomly into training (80%), development (10%), and test (10%) sets. At least 2 additional answers were collected for each question in the development and test sets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Top 10,000 Wikipedia articles were ranked using Project Nayuki's PageRanks; 536 articles were sampled uniformly at random. Individual paragraphs were extracted, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters. Answer types were categorized using constituency parses and POS tags from Stanford CoreNLP, with NER tags used to split proper noun phrases. Candidate answers were limited to constituents in the constituency parse; when correct answers were not constituents, the shortest constituent containing the correct answer was used as the target.
